newsitem.title: USA: Henkel bid for Loctite clears U.S. antitrust approval.
newsitem.headline: Henkel bid for Loctite clears U.S. antitrust approval.

text.p: Henkel KGaA said Monday that the U.S. government has approved the German chemicals and consumer products company's unsolicited $1.2 billion tender offer for full control of Loctite Corp.

Henkel, which early this month launched the $57.75 a share offer for the 65 percent stake in Loctite that it does not already own, said the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act expired on Friday.
The expiration implies the Federal Trade Commission has no antitrust concerns about the proposal.
Henkel's tender offer expires on Jan. 6.
Loctite, a Hartford, Conn.-based speciality adhesives maker, has spurned the bid as inadequate.
Takeover experts said Loctite itself had approached and been rejected by at least three possible "white knights," and said they believe the company will not find an alternative to Henkel's bid.
Yet, they also see Henkel ultimately boosting its offer by $2 to $3 per share to smooth its acquisition. A winning bid would be in the range of $59 to $61 per share, they said.
Loctite's stock fell 50 cents to close at $59.625 on the New York Stock exchange.
Unilever and Morton International Inc. were also mentioned as potential buyers, though it was unclear if they had been formally approached.
All of the companies declined to comment.

"It has been a quixotic search from the beginning because Henkel controls much of the company and because Loctite on a stand-alone basis is a very nichey type of company," said Morgan Stanley analyst Mark Gulley.
"The search (for a friendly merger partner) not bearing fruit is no surprise at all," he said, expressing surprise that Henkel and Loctite had not yet agreed on a deal.
"I suppose Henkel will have to sweeten their offer, but not by a lot" in order to make Loctite succumb, Gully said.
A second analyst, who declined to be named, said: "With Henkel's 35 percent, it is pretty hard to find a white knight. My guess is that it ends up friendly."
